key_insight: A rate-transfer framework turns finite-time Lyapunov bounds for an SDE into finite-time convergence rates for stochastic gradient methods.
engineering_relevance: This gives optimization practitioners a calculus-based route to prove and compare convergence rates for SGD-style algorithms, including new variants.
method: Model the stochastic gradient algorithm with an associated SDE.
Prove a Lyapunov generator inequality for the SDE using calculus.
Transfer the SDE finite-time bound into a convergence-rate guarantee for the discrete algorithm.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports that the method recovers established rates for classical stochastic gradient methods and extends to new algorithms via SDE-based calculus arguments.
watch_item: The approach depends on verifying suitable moment, smoothness, and Lyapunov conditions, which may be nontrivial for complex or non-smooth objectives.
paper_title: A Rate Transfer Method: Convergence Rates in Stochastic Gradient Descent via Stochastic Calculus
